findings.title: A time-bound fiduciary custody
findings.claim: The approach ban and best-manner exception govern access to an orphan's property before any taking; the 'until maturity' limit gives that duty an endpoint, while full covenant performance and answerability make the handoff accountable. Wider property connections sharpen the change: 4:2 forbids absorbing the estate into the guardian's own, 4:6 links maturity and sound judgment to delivery, 4:58 requires trusts returned to their owners with justice, and 70:32 pairs guarded trusts with covenant. Together they make the focus read as temporary stewardship aimed at restoring control, not merely avoiding theft.
findings.mechanism: The focus approach verb is governed by a prohibition and narrowed by an exception for the best manner; the orphan and property are its protected object. The maturity phrase sets the custody limit, and the following command to fulfill the covenant, repeated as an answerable subject, supplies the duty at exit. In 4:6, a life-stage marker, recognized sound judgment, and delivery occur in sequence; 4:2 bars consuming the estate together with one's own; 70:32 joins guarded trusts and covenant. Their contact turns proximity into regulated custody with an accountable handoff. The supplied reader-walk framing at 17:30 and 17:35-36 adds calibrated provision and measurable handling, while 2:282 supplies a wider written-and-witnessed analogue.
findings.reader_payoff: The exception becomes a narrow route for responsible care, not a license to treat the orphan's wealth as available. The time limit points toward the owner's eventual agency, and the covenant clause keeps the guardian answerable for how that interval is handled.
findings.containment: The ordinary prohibition, best-manner qualifier, maturity endpoint, and covenant sense remain recoverable. The global fiduciary image is an added relation, not a replacement or a claim that 17:34 states every procedure found elsewhere. In particular, 4:6's separate sound-judgment test is not imported as an express condition in this ayah, and 2:282's debt-writing rules are not imposed on every covenant. The best-mode phrase also appears for speech in 17:53 and response to hostility in 41:34; the reciprocal note preserves the possibility that 41:34 is a separate ethical domain, so the word alone does not prove the custody reading. Access-control, developmental custody, and auditability remain related but distinct readings.

branch_activations.independent_trigger: The prohibitive particle and the exception 'except by the best manner' shape the approach; 4:2 forbids absorbing the orphan's property and 4:6 regulates use and delivery.
branch_activations.activation: Because the approach itself is prohibited before a taking is completed, and the wider property rules distinguish proper care from absorption, the branch meets a preventive access boundary.
branch_activations.resulting_reading: The command governs entry into the handling of the asset before wrongful consumption, while the exception leaves a bounded route for care.
branch_activations.boundary: This is not a claim that all contact is forbidden: the ayah explicitly retains the best-manner exception, and the wider passages do not become procedures stated by 17:34.

findings.title: Fulfillment made reviewable
findings.claim: When the focus commands full performance of a covenant and then calls that covenant answerable, the supplied measure/accountability context and the wider writing-and-witnessing connection let completion be read as reviewable conduct, not inward intent alone.
findings.mechanism: The carrier is the full-performance verb and its covenant complement, returned to by the passive answerability predicate. The 17:35-36 reader-walk summary supplies measurement and accountable faculties; 2:282 supplies a wider transaction in which a fixed-term debt is written, witnessed, protected from shortfall, and handled for a weak party. Their contact makes covenant fulfillment visible as performance that can be checked. The 33:15 parallel repeats covenant answerability.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see how a commitment might be assessed through what was delivered and what can be accounted for, rather than treating fulfillment as an invisible intention.
findings.containment: The immediate measures may directly deepen orphan-property stewardship or remain adjacent controls in a broader ethical sequence; both readings stay live. The packet does not decide between them. 2:282 concerns debt documentation, not a procedure imposed on every covenant, and 83:2 shows that taking full measure can still be one-sided, so measurement alone does not guarantee justice.

epistemic.reason: The focus surface and exact Arabic for 2:282, 33:15, and 83:2 are supplied. The 17:35-36 contextual interpretation is legacy-unbound and target morphology is not present, so its contribution is qualified.

findings.title: Maturity and recognized capacity
findings.claim: Beside the focus's endpoint at full maturity, 4:6 keeps two thresholds distinct: reaching a life-stage marker and being recognized as sound in judgment before property is delivered. The wider comparison leaves a capacity-sensitive reading open alongside a chronological or bodily one.
findings.mechanism: The focus verb carries reaching and its object names maturity/strength; the 4:6 connection separately sequences reaching a life-stage, recognizing sound judgment, and delivering the orphan's property. Their contact makes maturity legible as a possible transfer-of-responsibility gate rather than only an age marker.
findings.reader_payoff: The endpoint can be perceived as a transition toward responsible agency, while the reader keeps both developmental timing and demonstrated capacity in view.
findings.containment: 17:34 does not state a competency test, numeric age, or financial/legal standard. The legal or financial-capacity extension is an inference from the property-transfer comparison, not an established gloss; 4:6 is not used to settle the chronological/physical alternative.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus occurrences and 4:6 Arabic are supplied, but the HFT nomination itself has no anchor evidence and the wider connection lacks target morphology. The comparison survives independently with that qualification.
